items.q: What is Grok Build, and what's under it?
items.a: xAI's agentic CLI for **Super Grok Heavy ($300/mo)**, harnessing **Grok 4.3** (~**500B** params). Artificial Analysis coding index: Grok **41** vs GPT 5.5 (**59**), Gemini 3.1 (**55**), Opus 4.7 (**53**) — intelligence index ~**53**, closer to frontier.

items.q: Did it get the BridgeMind stamp of approval?
items.a: **No** — two blockers: brutal **rate limits** and **Grok 4.3** output quality far behind frontier for design-heavy vibe coding.

items.q: How does Grok Build handle extreme sub-agent load?
items.a: **200 sub-agents** → CLI crash (`Thread SES panicked`). **50** → unstable; only a handful ran. **Claude Code at 100** → no crash; partitioned 582 files into **14 security domains** instead of literal 100 agents.

items.q: Does fast inference mean fast agent sessions?
items.a: No — Remotion plan took **24+ min** despite Grok's fast-model reputation. Session showed **512K** context (creator expected **1M+** for Grok 4.3).

Next.js revamp: **double nav bar**, weak pricing, "worse than Kimi K2.6." Remotion misaligned with real UI. Imagine infographic: low quality vs **GPT Image 2**. Debug plans OK; shipping UI/video not — **"GPT-4 type stuff."**

items.q: What does Grok Build do well as a harness?
items.a: **Zero-config Claude Code** plugin/skill/hook parity + AGENTS.md; praised plan-mode modal; built-in **Imagine** image gen (#2 ELO after GPT Image 2); fork/share/rewind/usage/dream/flush commands — still not enough without model quality.

items.q: How bad are Super Grok Heavy rate limits?
items.a: ~1 hour → **8% of a two-week quota** on **$300/mo**. Normal **6–8 hour** sessions would burn ~**50%** per session — incompatible with multi-agent fleets.

items.q: How should you evaluate agent CLIs?
items.a: Agent CLIs are a **commodity** — value = **subsidized access to the underlying model**. Grok Build loses to Claude Code (Opus 4.7) and Codex (GPT 5.5) on both quality and quota; **Grok 5** may change the trajectory.
